title: Contracts & Instruments
hook: MNQ isn't just a ticker on your screen. Know what you're actually trading.
mission: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to name the common futures instruments and explain the difference between a mini and a micro contract.

beats.heading: A standardized agreement
beats.body: A futures contract is a standardized agreement associated with buying or selling an underlying asset or financial benchmark, under specifications set by the exchange. When you trade futures, you're trading contracts whose values move with their underlying market — not buying shares of a company.

beats.heading: The instrument is the specific market
beats.body: Equity index futures include ES (E-mini S&P 500), MES (Micro E-mini S&P 500), NQ (E-mini Nasdaq-100), and MNQ (Micro E-mini Nasdaq-100). Metals include GC (Gold) and MGC (Micro Gold). Contract specifications differ — always verify current exchange specs before trading.

beats.heading: The pairs to know
beats.body: MNQ → Micro E-mini Nasdaq-100. NQ → E-mini Nasdaq-100. MES → Micro E-mini S&P 500. ES → E-mini S&P 500. MGC → Micro Gold. GC → Gold.

blocks.heading: NQ vs. MNQ — same family, different size
blocks.prompt: Tap each instrument to compare its contract multiplier.

left.label: MNQ
left.desc: Micro E-mini Nasdaq-100 — 1/10 the contract multiplier of NQ. Same underlying index exposure family, much smaller dollar risk.

right.label: NQ
right.desc: E-mini Nasdaq-100 — larger dollar exposure per point. 10x the contract multiplier of MNQ.

blocks.heading: What's wrong with this reasoning?
blocks.scenario: A trader moves from MNQ to NQ but keeps the same number of contracts because "the chart looks the same."

options.label: The contract multiplier is different, so the same price move produces very different P&L and risk
options.feedback: Exactly — the chart shape being similar doesn't mean the dollar exposure is similar.

options.label: Nothing — NQ and MNQ are the same size, just different tickers
options.feedback: They're not the same size — MNQ is 1/10 the contract multiplier of NQ.

blocks.quote: Never choose your number of contracts because someone else trades that size. Know the instrument. Know its value. Know your risk.

questions.question: Which pair correctly matches the instrument to its name?
questions.why: MGC is Micro Gold. ES is the full-size E-mini S&P 500 (MES is the micro), and MNQ is the micro version of NQ.

questions.question: A trader switches from trading 1 contract of MNQ to 5 contracts of MNQ. Has she changed instruments?
options: No — she's still trading MNQ; only her size and dollar exposure changed
Yes — 5 contracts makes it a different instrument
It's impossible to tell without knowing the price
questions.why: The instrument stays MNQ — contract count only changes exposure.

takeaways: A futures contract's value moves with its underlying market — it isn't ownership.
Micro contracts (MNQ, MES, MGC) are a fraction of their mini counterparts (NQ, ES, GC).
Contract count changes your exposure, not the instrument itself.
remember: Know the instrument. Know its value. Know your risk.
